option.label: Culm node densely bearded with spreading silvery hairs
option.detail: Inspect the actual culm node. Gould describes a dense silvery spreading beard; do not call these hairs the inner ligule. Uncertain printed hair-length unit is not used for scoring.

option.label: BOTH blade faces sometimes long-spreading-hairy
option.detail: Gould permits infrequent villosity on both blade surfaces; common plants are hairless or nearly so. This does not establish raised hair bases or a mandatory basal tuft.

option.label: Sheath sometimes villous with spreading hairs
option.detail: Gould permits infrequent long-spreading hairs on sheaths. Preserve the frequent hairless condition; do not require every plant to have hairy sheaths.

option.label: Dense erect cluster of silky-hairy flowering branches
option.detail: Gould describes2–7 conspicuously villous branches,2.5–6 cm, densely clustered and erect at the culm apex. Not a leaf hair tuft or culm-node beard.

option.label: Rachis and pedicels densely long-hairy
option.detail: Inspect flowering rachis and pedicels: narrow, densely villous, slightly flattened in Gould. Do not infer KR marginal cilia or a medial groove from general hairiness.

option.label: Sessile OUTER glume thin with rounded apex
option.detail: Locate the outer glume of the sessile spikelet. The thin rounded apex is not a lemma tip, glandular pit or automatic first-glume vein count.

option.label: Sessile OUTER glume: long hair line below apex
option.detail: Gould describes the rounded thin apex delimited by a line of long usually papilla-based hairs. Trace the hairs to the outer glume, not an adjacent blade or lemma.

option.label: Sessile OUTER glume: hairs down both back sides
option.detail: Gould continues the apical hair line down both sides of the dorsal surface. Do not recode this as KR stiff hairs only on the lower back.

option.label: Stalked OUTER glume: hair line across tip/down sides
option.detail: The awnless pedicelled companion is about as large as sessile one; its outer glume often has a line of hairs across the tip and down the sides. Keep both spikelets distinct.

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Follow the sessile outer-glume hair line
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould describes a thin rounded outer-glume apex edged by long usually papilla-based hairs, continuing down both sides of the back. The pedicelled outer glume often has a hair line across tip and down sides too.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: This exact pattern is more useful than a generic hairy head. KR first-glume lower-back hairs and blade papilla hairs are different positions; gland-pit or groove absence is not inferred.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact Gould p.588 organ/position mapping, not a new photograph identity certificate.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Dichanthium sericeum, printed p.588

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Separate node beard, ligule and flowering-axis villosity
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Nodes have dense spreading silvery hairs; true ligule is an erose1–2 mm membrane. Flowering rachis and pedicels are densely villous and slightly flattened;2–7 hairy branches cluster erect at the tip.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: The node beard is not a ligule. Sheaths and both blade faces can be hairless or infrequently spreading-villous. Node-hair length unit is held for confirmation.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Gould p.588; variation and distinct anatomical sites preserved.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Dichanthium sericeum, printed p.588

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Compare the paired spikelets and keep the awn-unit hold visible
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Sessile spikelets2.5–3.5 mm, with dark twisted twice-geniculate lemma awns; similar-sized stalked partners awnless. The supplied image appears to print2–3.5 mm for awn length, while VicFlora subsp.sericeum reports2–3 cm.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Do not silently turn mm into cm or use this discrepancy to certify an exact short-awn match/exclusion. Australian subspecies evidence does not certify a Texas plant.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Book measurement-unit discrepancy unresolved; structural book path can still be tested.
